- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, then decay too slowly — suggesting lag in recognizing downward momentum.
- After a spike in price (e.g., 72+), model often overreacts and forecasts higher than true outcome, then undercorrects.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model fails to anticipate sharp declines after peaks.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when recent history includes high prices.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — fails to adjust downward when recent 30d includes multiple high values.
- Correction should reduce forecast by 5–15% for periods with recent high prices (last 5–10 days of history).
- When true outcome drops below 65, model often still forecasts above 68 — apply downward bias adjustment.
- Avoid forecasting above 70 when history includes 3+ consecutive days above 70 — model tends to overreact.
- Use moving average of last 7 days as a sanity check — if forecast exceeds 1.5x that, reduce by 20–30%.
